note: What the battle leaves on the table (the advanced options Show hulks and Show craters): a hulk where a vehicle is destroyed, a crater where a fire mission lands, each a drawing printed into the board on its hex, under the counters. No rule reads them. `hulks`: which pictures (assets/marks/v1/marks.json) a destroyed unit leaves, by the kind of unit its counter carries (the unit data's `kind`: content/units/*.units.yaml, and the reference ruleset's unit ids, which its counters carry as their kind); where two fit, a seeded choice between them. `none`: the kinds that leave nothing, named so that no kind is left to a default. `craters`: a landed mission's seeded choice. `size`: a mark's longer side, in h (a hex is 1 h across its flats). `place`: where a mark lies in its hex, from the hex's middle, in h (x right, y down the board, toward the hex's lower flat, away from its number at the top): a hex's first mark lies to one side and its second to the other, `across` from the middle and `down` (a seeded share of the range) below it, a seeded `jitter` either way, turned a seeded share of `turnDeg` either way. `perHex`: the most that lie in a hex (a newer one takes the place of the older of its kind, else of the oldest). `look`: how each kind is printed into the board (scene/marks/model.ts, MarkLook: opacity; shadows lifted; colour kept; inked toward the board's key ink or an ink of its own; edge softened; a light halo; laid on as ink, multiply, or over the board, normal: the hulks' blend serves both). `ease`: the seconds a mark takes to fade in where it is laid, the seconds after a mission lands before its crater, and the seconds the marks of a kind take to go or come when its option is switched.

hulks.why: Turreted tanks: either tank. The sloped tank with its turret thrown off beside it reads as a tank at a glance (only a turreted vehicle can lose one); the boxy tank under its smoke is a tank as well.
Turretless armor: the boxy tank alone, its low square hull the nearest the sheet has to a casemate; never the thrown turret, which a vehicle without one cannot lose.
An open-topped gun carriage on a tank's tracks: the boxy tank, or the green open-topped hull half buried in earth.
An open-topped armored body: the green hull half buried in earth, whose running gear (wheels in front, tracks behind) the earth hides.

none.why: Infantry and towed guns and mortars leave no hulk; nor does a horse-drawn wagon (the sheet has no picture of one, and the truck's would say a truck died there).
